core_obligations: Record the field-theoretic equivalence of conditions (2) and (3) (proof lines 1457-1459).

From (1) to (2): express the local ring at the generic point as the filtered colimit of the rings of nonempty affine opens and combine the local criterion with the subalgebra statement to get geometric irreducibility of that local ring, then pass to its residue field using that the kernel is locally nilpotent (proof lines 1461-1473).

From (2) to (1): reduce to X reduced, take a nonempty affine open with coordinate ring a domain whose fraction field is the residue field at xi, and use the subalgebra statement to conclude that the coordinate ring is geometrically irreducible; the local criterion then gives geometric irreducibility of X (proof lines 1475-1483).
proof_roadmap: Equivalence of (2) and (3) by a field-theoretic criterion (proof lines 1457-1459).
From X to its function field through the local ring (proof lines 1461-1473).
From the function field back to X through an affine chart (proof lines 1475-1483).
difficulty_reason: For an irreducible scheme X over k with generic point xi, the lemma proves the equivalence of geometric irreducibility of X, geometric irreducibility of the residue field at the generic point, and the separable algebraic closure of k inside that field being k itself (statement lines 1445-1454). The equivalence of the second and third conditions is a field-theoretic input. The proof of the remaining implications uses the local ring at the generic point as the bridge: it is the filtered colimit of the rings of nonempty affine opens, so geometric irreducibility is inherited from the colimit argument one way and, in the other direction, a subalgebra of a geometrically irreducible algebra is geometrically irreducible, which passes from the residue field down to each affine chart and then back to X (proof lines 1456-1483). The pass between the local ring and its residue field uses that the kernel is locally nilpotent (proof lines 1469-1473). The claim is H2: three cited algebra inputs plus one reduction through an affine chart, with the colimit and subalgebra steps as the content.
